neighbours.label: the preposition or 'to' completing an adjective or participle (capable of, unable to, faced with, doomed to)
fire: Very few birds are capable of flying that far without rest.
The rescue team was unable to reach the village before dark.
Small farms faced with rising costs have started to sell land.
Without reform the program seems doomed to fail within a decade.
Many students are unaware of the grants available to them.
The old bridge is no longer fit for heavy traffic.
Some patients become dependent on painkillers after surgery.
The village, cut off from the main road, relies on boats.
quiet: Very few birds fly that far over the open sea in winter.
The rescue team finally reached the village late at night.
Small farms in the north have started to sell their land.
Without reform the program will close within a decade.
Many students in the city have applied for the new grants.
The old bridge near the mill was closed last week.
Some patients at the clinic take painkillers after surgery.
The village near the main road has a busy market.

notes: card flags broad (4.1%) and gate-closed regime; locative prepositions read up to 0.16 in probes
